narrative:
Your law school application was denied because the model estimated an 84% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a high estimated risk, not a certainty, but it was enough to drive the rejection.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing. You are in the lowest decile, while accepted students average around the sixth decile; this difference weighed heavily toward predicting bar failure. The next most important factor was your law school admission test score of 20, far below the accepted-student average of about 37, which also pushed the prediction toward failure. Your first-year standing was the third most influential factor. At the fifth decile it is somewhat below the accepted average of sixth, but relative to the other factors it leaned toward passing. Your middle family-income bracket and full-time status were less influential.

To move forward, ask admissions for the specific reconsideration or appeal process, verify that your record and scores are accurate, and speak with an academic advisor about a concrete bar-readiness plan. Retaking the law school admission test and strengthening your academic record, especially later-year performance, would address the two strongest concerns. You may also consider programs with conditional admission or additional bar preparation support, and request feedback before reapplying.
